questions.question_text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G earned distinct marks. A scored more than B, C and D; G scored more than E and F; and F scored more than A. Who scored highest?
questions.explanation: The clues give G above F, F above A, and A above B, C and D; G is also above E. Thus G is highest.
questions.source: Puzzle 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 7; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Seven boys B1–B7 have distinct weights. B4 is lighter than exactly three boys. B1 is heavier than B7; B2 is heaviest; B5 and B6 are each heavier than B1; and B3 is lighter than B7. How many boys are lighter than B1?
questions.explanation: B2, B5 and B6 are already heavier than B1. For exactly three boys to be heavier than B4, B1 must be lighter than B4. Below B1 are B7 and B3.
questions.source: Puzzle 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 9; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Seven spheres V1–V7 have distinct volumes. V4 is smaller than V1, V2 and V5. Exactly two spheres have smaller volume than V7, and V4 is larger than V7. V6 is not the smallest. How many spheres have smaller volume than V3?
questions.explanation: V1, V2 and V5 are above V4, and V4 is above V7. Since exactly two spheres are below V7 and V6 is not the smallest, V3 is the smallest; none is below it.
questions.source: Puzzle 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 10; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Seven boys B1–B7 have distinct IQ scores. B2 is above B6; B5 has the third-lowest IQ; B4 has the highest IQ; B3 is below B2; B1 is above B2; and B7 has the lowest IQ. Who has the second-highest IQ?
questions.explanation: B4 is highest. B1 is above B2, and B2 is above B6 and B3, so B1 must be second-highest.
questions.source: Puzzle 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 11; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Seven students P, Q, R, S, T, U and V have distinct marks. P is second-highest; V is above only one student; S scored more than T but less than P; exactly three students scored more than T and three less; neither R nor Q has the lowest score. Who has the lowest score?
questions.explanation: T is fourth and P second. S must be third. V is second-lowest, while neither Q nor R is lowest; therefore U is lowest.
questions.source: Puzzle 01_ Class Notes.pdf, page 12; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: D, E, F, H, I, J and K have exams on distinct days Monday–Sunday. K is Thursday and E Saturday. H is immediately before I; D immediately after I; F is after J. How many people have exams between F and D?
questions.explanation: The H–I–D block must be Monday–Wednesday. K is Thursday and E Saturday; J is Friday and F Sunday. K, J and E lie between D and F.
questions.source: Puzzle 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 4; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V have exams on distinct days Monday–Sunday. Q is immediately before T, and T immediately before P. P is Wednesday. R is neither Saturday nor Sunday. U is Friday and S immediately follows U. Who has the Sunday exam?
questions.explanation: Q and T are Monday and Tuesday, followed by P Wednesday. U and S are Friday and Saturday. R must be Thursday, leaving V for Sunday.
questions.source: Puzzle 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 5; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G have exams on distinct days Monday–Sunday. Exactly two exams are before F; A is immediately after F; E is not Sunday; G is immediately before E and has the Friday exam; C is not Monday; D is immediately before F; and exactly one exam is between A and E. Who has the Monday exam?
questions.explanation: F is Wednesday, D Tuesday and A Thursday. G Friday and E Saturday. C cannot be Monday, so C is Sunday and B is Monday.
questions.source: Puzzle 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 6; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: B, E, Y, O, N, D and S have interviews on distinct days Monday–Sunday. Exactly three interviews are before D. E is after O and before S. Y is after N and before B. N is after D. How many interviews are between Y and E?
questions.explanation: D is Thursday. The remaining constraints force N Friday, Y Saturday and B Sunday, while E lies on Tuesday; three interviews separate E and Y.
questions.source: Puzzle 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 7; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: L, M, N, O, P, Q and R have exams on distinct days Monday–Sunday. O is immediately after Q; M is immediately after O and has the Wednesday exam. Exactly two days lie between L and R. N is not immediately before R, and P is immediately after N. When does N have the exam?
questions.explanation: Q Monday, O Tuesday and M Wednesday. The remaining clues allow two full schedules, but in both N is Friday.
questions.source: Puzzle 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 4; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: N, E, A, T, L and Y occupy six distinct floors numbered 1 (lowest) to 6. L is immediately above Y. Exactly two people live between Y and E, with E on an odd floor below Y. A is immediately below N. How many people live between T and N?
questions.explanation: E must be on floor 1, Y on 4 and L on 5. A and N occupy floors 2 and 3, leaving T on 6. Two people are between T and N.
questions.source: Puzzle 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 8; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: G, H, J, K, L and P live on floors 1–6, with 1 lowest. J is on an even floor other than 4, with two people between J and L. P is on an odd floor other than 1, with two people between P and G. K is immediately below P. How many people live between H and K?
questions.explanation: The only arrangement from floor 1 upward is H, G, L, K, P, J. Two people are between H and K.
questions.source: Puzzle 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 9; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V live on floors 1–7. Q lives on floor 2; R is on the top floor; R is immediately above U; S is immediately below V; three people live between T and P; and one person lives between R and P. On which floor does P live?
questions.explanation: R is floor 7, so P is floor 5. The remaining clues fill U6, V4, S3, Q2 and T1.
questions.source: Puzzle 02_ Class Notes.pdf, page 12; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: A, B, C, D, E and F live on floors 1–6. F is even-numbered but not floor 4, with two people between F and B. A is immediately below E, and E is on an even floor. Neither A nor D lives on floor 1. Who lives on floor 4?
questions.explanation: The only assignment from floor 1 upward is C, F, A, E, B, D. E occupies floor 4.
questions.source: Puzzle 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 5; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Seven boxes E, F, G, H, K, L and M are stacked top to bottom. Exactly two boxes are below E; exactly one is above H; one box is between H and G; L is immediately above M; and K is somewhere below F. How many boxes are between F and L?
questions.explanation: The unique stack from top to bottom is F, H, K, G, E, L, M. Four boxes lie between F and L.
questions.source: Puzzle 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 6; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Seven boxes A–G are stacked top to bottom. Exactly two boxes are below G; one is above B; one lies between B and D; A is immediately above C; and E is below F. Which box is topmost?
questions.explanation: The only stack top to bottom is F, B, A, D, C, G, E. F is topmost.
questions.source: Puzzle 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 7; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Seven boxes D, E, F, H, I, J and K are stacked top to bottom. J is second from the bottom; three boxes are between J and E; K is below J; F is the only box between E and H; and D is above E. How many boxes are between I and K?
questions.explanation: The stack is D, E, F, H, I, J, K. One box, J, lies between I and K.
questions.source: Puzzle 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 8; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: K, L, M, N and P receive salaries on dates 1–5 of the same month. L is paid immediately after M; N immediately before K; P immediately after K; and P is paid on date 3. On which date is M paid?
questions.explanation: N is paid on date 1, K on 2, P on 3, M on 4 and L on 5.
questions.source: Puzzle 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 9; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Madhu, Anshul, Avni, Aarav, Preeti and Shikha present on distinct dates from March 11–16. Anshul presents March 14; Shikha is the day before Anshul. Exactly one person presents between Shikha and Preeti, with Preeti earlier. Shikha is before Avni, and Avni is immediately before Madhu. Who presents on March 15?
questions.explanation: Shikha is on the 13th, Anshul on the 14th. Preeti must be on the 11th; Avni and Madhu are on the 15th and 16th. Aarav is on the 12th.
questions.source: Puzzle 03_ Class Notes.pdf, page 10; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Six parcels A–F have distinct weights. B is heavier than A and C; D is lighter than A; E is heavier than B; F is lighter than C. Who is heaviest?
questions.explanation: The chain E>B>A>C>F and A>D places E at the top.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Seven runners A–G finish in distinct positions. A finishes before B and C; D finishes immediately after A; E finishes after C; F finishes before A; and G finishes after E. Who finishes fourth?
questions.explanation: The clues place F,A,D before B/C, and E,G after C. The unique order is F,A,D,C,B,E,G.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Seven students A–G rank by score, highest first. E is highest; A is second; B is immediately below A; C is immediately below B; D is immediately below C; F is immediately below D; and G is last. Who is second-lowest?
questions.explanation: The full order is E, A, B, C, D, F, G. F is second-lowest.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Six interviews for A–F are scheduled Monday through Saturday, one per day. A is Monday, B is Tuesday, C is Wednesday, D is Thursday, E is Friday and F is Saturday. Who is scheduled Wednesday?
questions.explanation: The stated schedule places C on Wednesday.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Seven workshops for A–G run Monday–Sunday. E is Monday; A is Tuesday; D is Wednesday; B is Thursday; C is Friday; F is Saturday; and G is Sunday. Who is scheduled Sunday?
questions.explanation: The stated schedule places G on Sunday.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Five friends A–E live on floors 1–5, with 1 lowest. A lives on floor 2, B immediately above A, C above B, D below A and E on the top floor. Who lives on floor 4?
questions.explanation: The order from floor 1 upward is D, A, B, C, E. C is on floor 4.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Seven residents A–G live on floors 1–7, with floor 1 lowest. D is on floor 1; E is immediately above D; A is on an odd floor above floor 1; B is immediately above A; C is two floors above B; F is on floor 5; and G is on floor 7. Who lives on floor 4?
questions.explanation: The conditions place D,E on floors 1,2. A must be floor 3 so that B is floor 4 and C floor 6; F and G occupy floors 5 and 7.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Six boxes A–F are stacked top to bottom. B is immediately below A; C is below B; D is immediately above E; and F is below C. If exactly one box lies between C and D, which box is topmost?
questions.explanation: The constraints give the unique stack A, B, C, D, E, F; A is topmost.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Five events A–E occur on dates 1–5, one per date. A is on date 1; B is immediately after A; C is after B; D is immediately before E; and C is immediately before D. Which event is on date 4?
questions.explanation: The sequence is A, B, C, D, E, so D occurs on date 4.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Six project presentations A–F are scheduled Monday through Saturday, one per day. A is immediately before B; C is two days after B; D is immediately after C; E is before A; and F is Saturday. Who presents on Thursday?
questions.explanation: The unique schedule is E, A, B, F, C, D from Monday through Saturday, so F presents Thursday.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question

questions.question_text: Seven boxes A–G are stacked top to bottom. D is topmost; E is bottommost; B is immediately below D; C is immediately below B; F is immediately below C; A is immediately below F; and G is immediately below A. How many boxes are between C and G?
questions.explanation: The unique stack is D, B, C, F, A, G, E. F and A lie between C and G.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question
